title: Scheduled Rotation Evidence Stream Generator for Cross-Region Residency and Retention
creator: Claire Huang
description: Implement a scheduled evidence-generation pipeline that captures cryptographic state snapshots (key metadata, rotation history, KMS/HSM provenance, and retention policy application) and streams tamper-evident bundles to our audit export queue. The generator must operate across regions and tenant groupings, respect per-tenant residency and retention settings, and produce standardized signed artifacts for downstream compliance reporting. This ticket covers design, implementation, end-to-end tests, and a phased rollout with emergency rollback instructions.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled job produces signed evidence bundles for each tenant group at configured cadence (daily/weekly) and pushes them to audit-export queue.

Bundles include: key id, key version, creation/rotation timestamps, KMS/HSM provider metadata, KMS key ARN/resource, rotation-trigger metadata (automatic/manual), residency tags, retention policy snapshot, and toolchain version used to produce the bundle.
Each bundle is integrity-protected (signed) and verifiable by the audit service using a stable verification key; verification must detect tampering and missing fields.
Generator respects tenant data residency (region scoping) and does not include cross-region key material; test matrix covers tenants with single-region, multi-region, and private/on-prem setups.
End-to-end integration tests exercise KMS mock providers and an HSM emulator; test artifacts are uploaded to the compliance test bucket and validated by the compliance runner.
Performance: generating evidence for 10k tenants (sampling mode) completes within the scheduled window (2 hours) using autoscaled workers and bounded memory per worker.
Operational runbook and playbook checked into Confluence with rollback, failure modes, and contact matrix.
Security review completed and signoff attached in PR description.
progress_updates: 2026-01-18: Spike completed comparing existing attestation formats. Chose compact JSON-LD envelope with detachable signature to keep artifacts small and compatible with archive systems.
2026-02-02: Prototype generator wired to KMS SDK and HSM shim. Verified we can fetch rotation history and metadata without accessing plaintext key material.

2026-02-16: Integration tests adapted to use HSM emulator (SoftHSM) and a local KMS stub. Found a race condition when retrieving rotation events during concurrent rotations; added read-consistent snapshotting to the design.

2026-02-28: Security review kickoff with InfoSec. Raised question about storing verification public key in the audit export; decided to publish signing key fingerprint and rotate verification key via a separate key-publish job.
2026-03-05: Load test for evidence generation at 2.5k tenants completed. Observed CPU spike during JSON signing; moved signing to a worker pool and introduced batching for metadata queries.
2026-03-10: Implementation branch opened (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4289). End-to-end smoke tests passing in staging for single-region tenants.
decisions: Use detached JWS signatures (compact) rather than full PKCS7 bundles to keep artifacts small and allow external verification with standard JWT tooling.
Snapshot rotational state using the KMS/HSM read-only audit API and a consistent read token to avoid capturing partial rotations.
Store evidence bundle metadata in S3-like object store with tenant-scoped prefixes and write-once object lifecycle; objects flagged for long-term retention are copied to the compliance vault bucket.
Do not include any secret key material or KV cache contents in bundles; only include non-secret metadata and provenance references.
Expose a dry-run mode that generates bundles but does not push to the export queue for testing and compliance validation.
notes: Follow-up: coordinate with Dedicated infra to ensure collector worker nodes have access to KMS endpoints in private clusters.
Follow-up: add a per-tenant opt-out flag and ensure product/PM signoff for default cadence for large customers.
Edge case: tenants with on-prem HSMs require a pull-based connector; added a sub-issue to implement a secure pull gateway (ENG-55910).
Monitoring: add SLO for bundle delivery success rate and a reconciliation job that compares expected cadence to delivered artifacts.
